decision: Six-shot, 20-frame exception for clips 01–12; three-shot CTA exception for clip 13. Each shot contributes a distinct causal story beat after r002 repeated views and unclear symbols. Narration/timing unchanged.

beats: Macro low angle: the single ornate crown rests above the much larger dark carved city relief, with sea-blue inset and the seven tiny island tokens visible only as a compact cluster at lower right. Crown gives scale; no person enters.
Overhead medium: the crown is at upper left; the city-shaped relief fills most of frame while one flat island token sits at its edge. The token slides fully inside the outline and stops.
Oblique close: seven separate flat island tokens lie in one tidy row inside the relief. The camera holds long enough to read seven distinct shapes, not wax cylinders, candles, or fingers.
Top-down wide: all seven identical tokens fit comfortably within the one city silhouette; the surrounding blank table remains dark. The crown stays small at upper edge.
Macro of a single island token lifted from that seven-token row by a simple flat outlined wooden pointer, never a human finger; the other six remain in place.
Hard-cut graphic view of that same isolated island silhouette against flat illustrated sea-blue space within the relief; one tiny landmass centered and completely still by the end.

High wide from the approved overlook: one compact Elba harbor occupies the lower third and an immense outlined blue sea fills the upper frame; Napoleon is a tiny black-bicorne silhouette at lower left.
Closer shoreline insert from the same viewpoint: warm terracotta roofs, stone quay and one two-masted harbor vessel establish a real inhabited island, with every roof and wave drawn and outlined.
Low three-quarter back view at the stone rail: one Napoleon boot and navy coat are visible; he plants one boot and settles, still at frame left. No disembodied boot overlay.
Tight silhouette: the single black bicorne and compact round head rise above the stone rail, sunlit rim at upper left; face still mostly concealed.
Clear three-quarter portrait of exactly one Napoleon: dot eyes, angled brows, closed mouth, gold-edged bicorne, navy coat with red cuffs and hand tucked at coat. He turns toward the sea once.
Wide return to the same overlook: Napoleon stands left, compact Elba town below, sea behind; camera locked and he holds the recognizable emperor silhouette through final frame.

Wide winter courtyard: three coalition figures stand together at left while lone Napoleon stands separated at right; the fallen imperial standard crosses the foreground diagonal. Cold slate sky and outlined mud.
Low close of the single imperial standard pole already lying on the ground; its red-white-blue cloth settles once in the same outlined mud, making defeat explicit.
Reverse medium on three coalition figures, distinct uniform silhouettes, no bicornes; the central official takes one deliberate step toward Napoleon.
Tight portrait of Napoleon alone: his identical bicorne and round off-white face fill frame; angled brows lower and shoulders remain upright, no attack or injury.
Low view along the fallen standard toward Napoleon and the closed iron gate: his boots remain planted while the coalition line fills the far side. Clear power reversal.
Wide settled tableau returns: three coalition figures left, one Napoleon right, fallen standard foreground. All hold still at the gate; no second battle or execution begins.
Wide table geometry: three officials on left face one Napoleon on right across the one blank parchment; city visible through window. One official glances from Napoleon toward the city.
Close of an official outlined mitten placing a sheathed sword DOWN beside the parchment, away from Napoleon; the sword stays sheathed and still.

Over-shoulder of one official toward the existing city window: the distant civilian streets fill background while the official pauses, visibly weighing public reaction. No new crowd or paper portrait.
Tight reaction of Napoleon in the same seat and same hat: upright posture, closed mouth, one hand at coat; his presence remains politically powerful.
Macro of one official glove sliding the same blank parchment into the open central table space; no writing appears.
Overhead two sides of the bargain: official hand at left and Napoleon glove at right stop on opposite edges of the one blank parchment; sheathed sword remains outside the center.
Wide chamber composition: all three officials left, Napoleon right, the tiny isolated island and huge mainland relief visibly between them. Official points to tiny island once.
Tight recognizable Napoleon portrait, gold-edged black bicorne already on his one head; his single outlined glove touches its brim, confirming he keeps imperial title.
Overhead from the same table: the one small tan Elba island is isolated in blue sea on Napoleon side; the large mainland relief remains at official side, both shapes fixed.
Close on an official mitten tracing the broad EMPTY blue water gap from the little island toward mainland, then stopping before the mainland. No bridge, boat or crossing.
Two-shot across the table: Napoleon turns his dot eyes from the large mainland to the one tiny island; his hat and uniform do not change, officials stay left.
Final low tabletop tableau: tiny Elba and huge mainland remain separated by broad blue water; Napoleon sits beyond the island in his bicorne, visually trapped there. Hold still.
Close from Napoleon side: the tiny Elba island and distant large mainland remain apart on the table; Napoleon looks down with sharply angled brows.
Medium on one Napoleon opposite the same three officials; he lowers his hand from his bicorne onto the blank deal parchment, a single reluctant acceptance gesture.
Overhead detail: his one glove stays pressed on the blank parchment beside the island, while mainland remains untouched across the blue gap.
Instant hard cut to warm Elba quay. The same one Napoleon stands beside the approved moored vessel and compact harbor buildings; full figure recognizable, boat at frame left.
Low boot-and-stone insert derived from same quay: Napoleon plants exactly one black boot on sunlit quay stones beside a single mooring rope; no second person.
Medium wide of Napoleon at the quay looking toward the compact town with hand at coat; vessel stays moored behind. He settles into his new island role before the final frame.
Wide workshop: one Napoleon at frame left and one baker at right, the white flag with red diagonal and three gold bees flat on the front workbench; Napoleon points toward flag once.
Tight overhead flag insert: red diagonal band and exactly three separate gold bees fill the frame; a single outlined mitten smooths one fold so the design is readable.
Medium two-shot on same baker and Napoleon: Napoleon points with one simplified glove to one round dough loaf while baker watches, mouth closed; oven behind.
Tight oven-side close: the one baker guides one formed loaf from workbench toward the brick oven opening, one complete motion; flour is simple outlined specks.
Instant hard cut to finished pale-stone hospital exterior. One headscarf caregiver carrying folded bandages approaches open wide doorway; two clean white beds visible inside.
Closer doorway view: the caregiver pauses at threshold facing exactly one resting patient in the farther bed; second bed empty, folded bandages on shelf, purpose unambiguous. Hold still.
Wide approved parade yard: Napoleon stands left of one shako officer; two compact rows of outlined soldiers behind them, with the single two-masted brig small in harbor background.
Low side view of one orderly row of distinct shako soldiers; a single front boot comes to attention while the rest remain still.
High yard view: several short ranks occupy only a corner of the stone court, leaving generous empty space; Napoleon stays unique at the front. Small army scale reads.
Medium Napoleon and shako officer two-shot: officer points from the ranks toward the one distant brig; Napoleon turns his dot eyes toward it.
Close of one mooring line attached to that same two-masted brig in the outlined harbor; rope tightens once, water remains flat painted shapes.
Clear full-profile portrait of precisely one two-masted wooden brig at Elba harbor, entire hull and both masts visible, with compact soldiers on quay for scale.
Macro of a recognizably horse-shaped small brown wooden figurine on the approved tabletop; three similar horse pieces can be seen behind, stable legs and outlined painted grain.
Oblique wide of the same strategy table: horse pieces and a compact cluster of tiny Elba soldier counters at near edge, enormous ranks of red and blue France counters at far edge.
Low close on the single black-bicorne Napoleon figurine leading the tiny Elba group; a vast wall of inert counters looms beyond. The figurine slides forward once.
High overhead contrast: tiny Elba group occupies a thumb-sized corner, the larger French counter field spans nearly the whole table; an existing narrow gap is visible through it.
Tight gap insert: the Napoleon figurine passes between two stationary large-counter rows without contact, sword strike, blood or battle.
Wide tabletop payoff: tiny group is now on the far side of the unbroken mass of larger counters; French counters remain upright and still. The paradox is clear and resolved.
Top-down tabletop: many small France population counters fill most of the map relief while a tiny Elba group occupies only a corner; no writing or literal numerals.
Raking low view across the dense France counters to the few Elba counters; distance and scale make thirty million versus a small force intuitive. Nothing moves.
Hard cut to Elba quay: the one recognizable Napoleon in bicorne pivots toward the single two-masted brig moored beside him; soldiers wait in compact line.
Gangplank close: one shako soldier steps from stone quay onto the one brig, and the short line follows behind; all remain illustrated stick people.
Low hull-and-mast view of the same single brig: two masts, pale sails, black/navy hull; the mooring line is released once while Napoleon is aboard.
Wide three-quarter departure: exactly one brig moves a short distance from Elba quay, Napoleon and small party aboard, illustrated town behind; boat settles in frame before cut.
Wide illustrated French shore: the one two-masted brig is close offshore and its one gangplank leads to sand; Napoleon is first at its foot, small party behind.
Low close of Napoleon single black boot stepping from gangplank onto French sand; the same outlined brig remains visible behind to establish cause and place.
Medium front Napoleon portrait on shore with bicorne, red cuffs and hand at coat; two Elba soldiers stand behind as he looks inland.
Hard cut to mountain road: Napoleon in foreground, compact party behind him, broad French line across the entire road in distance. Both sides stop.
Low reverse from behind French shako soldiers: several ranks recede upward, muskets at rest, one lone recognizable Napoleon far below at center.
Wide face-off: large French force blocks road with an unbroken line; one Napoleon and tiny party halt at safe distance. No weapon raised, no shot. Hold.
Tight soldier reaction from French front line: one shako soldier looks at the single familiar Napoleon in background and visibly relaxes his shoulders.
Medium two soldiers at same barrier lower their muskets together, barrels pointing to ground; both faces remain simple and mouths shut.
High wide road composition: first pair of soldiers step sideways, leaving one clear human-width corridor through the formerly unbroken line.
Centered low view: exactly one Napoleon walks one step through the open corridor; ranks stay still and no one attacks.
Hard cut to Paris arch and cobbled street: the same one Napoleon leads a compact column through the arch toward the palace skyline, warm evening light.
Medium at end of arch: Napoleon reaches the palaceward threshold, recognizable black bicorne and coat still intact, companions behind. He stops before entrance, setting up next clip.
Frames 0–8, 0.000–0.375s: tight palace doorway from Picture 2; one brass handle completes a single turn, guard stays off to side, no button yet.
Frames 9–20, 0.375–0.875s: exactly one Napoleon enters the open palace doorway, one clear step; shako guard remains at side, no button yet.

Frames 21–119, 0.875–5.000s: INSTANT hard cut to the exact approved Picture 1 Paris-window tableau. One Napoleon stands left of window with hand at coat; one red rounded button at lower-middle 67% frame height already reads exactly SUBSCRIBE in white uppercase, one line. The button and spelling never change. From frame 51 through 119, every pixel, camera, light and subject remains static.
